title: Whether SCDF is taking steps to reduce vegetation fires as temperatures rise
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether the SCDF is taking precautionary steps to reduce vegetation fires, given more vegetation fires since 2022 and Singapore's rising annual average temperature.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said climate change has brought drier, hotter weather and higher wildfire risk, and that the SCDF leads an inter-agency Wildfire Task Force with SLA, NParks, NEA and PUB. The Task Force monitors weather patterns and starts preventive measures before expected dry spells, including spotting hotspots, watering and trimming overgrown vegetation, creating fire breaks or buffer zones, and public education on not discarding lighted materials. He said vegetation fires have generally been kept under control at under 200 a year over the last five years, but noted 2019 saw numbers in the 800s during sustained dry weather. He said the situation is seasonal and depends on rainfall, so vigilance and proactive measures are needed, especially when the Meteorological Service forecasts dry weather.

key_points.quote: educating the public not to indiscriminately discard lighted materials, such as cigarette butts, onto grass patches

key_points.quote: the number of vegetation fires has generally been kept under control – under 200 per year over the last five years
